## What the Papercup is

The Papercup is **one role**, not two cooperating hats
(`papercup-herald-2026-06-21` D-001). Watching the fleet is simply *how* it knows
what to tell the user — same identity. It is:

- **always-on, voice-first** — the same live converse + ElevenLabs voice brain the
  legacy "operator" ran, re-homed onto the `papercup` role (D-006: re-home, not
  rewrite — only the three hardcoded `'operator'` bindings were parameterized).
- **short, status + suggestions** — reuse the operator reply caps (~220 chars for
  voice, terse for text). The Papercup answers "what's the fleet doing / what
  should I work on next," and for anything that needs a real plan its move is
  "want me to hand this to the Mug?" — it is **not** the deep-planning agent
  (D-004).
- **never the placer** — the Mug is the brain/placer; the Papercup suggests and
  hands off but **never spawns/places/cancels** (D-002). This is enforced
  structurally by the capability envelope (`ROLE_ENVELOPES.papercup` denies
  fs-write/bash/spawn/place/kill), not by convention — an envelope test asserts the
  Papercup cannot place or execute.

The boundary with the other autonomous roles: the **Mug** steers and places, the
**Overwatch** is the machine-facing supervisor, and the **Papercup** is the
human-facing narrator. The legacy "operator" role was decomposed into those three;
only the machine-facing halves shipped, and this plan re-homes the orphaned
human-facing concierge brain onto the Papercup.

## How to enable it

Two independent toggles, deliberately decoupled (D-015):

1. **`PAPERCUP` feature flag** (wire value `papercusp-sentinel` — kept pre-rename,
   not yet migrated to a `papercusp-papercup` key) — gates the **settings UI**
   (plus the `papercup` role registration and its autonomous wake-loop). When on,
   the Papercup tab appears in the operator-vite left sidebar (`LeftSidebar.tsx`
   `TABS`, after Overwatch), with the exact OVERWATCH treatment: a `visibleTabs`
   filter + a `?lst=papercup` stale-deep-link snap-back to a default tab when the
   flag is off. Flipping the flag shows/hides the tab; it does **not** by itself
   repoint the brain. **As of `voice-unified-sentinel-pipeline-2026-07-01` P-011
   the runtime default flipped to ON** (the live-run proof landed 2026-06-24; the
   Papercup pane is now the one voice brain, so leaving it dark would mean a dead
   voice product) — flip it OFF via `/admin/features` to go dark. The sibling
   `PAPERCUP_PROACTIVE` flag (wire value `papercusp-sentinel-proactive`, also
   runtime-default ON) separately gates the server-side proactive "decide to
   speak" sweep described below.
2. **`humanFacingRole` voice pref** (`'operator'` | `'papercup'`, default
   **`'operator'`**) — this is the real switch that **repoints the live brain**. It
   lives in the voice prefs (it is one of `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`), and
   `resolveConfig → ElSessionConfig → start` sets `brainRole` from it. The
   ElevenLabs agent id / signed-URL are unchanged — only which persona + read-context
   the converse loop loads changes. The operator persona stays as a flagged
   migration fallback (D-006).

The role threads end-to-end: `role?: string` (default `'operator'`) flows through
`converse.ts` → `converse-prompt.ts` → the three persona loaders, and through the
voice seam (`askOperator(question, conversationId, role)`) and the text/mobile
paths (`operator-converse.ts` + device routes fall back to `humanFacingRole`; an
explicit body `role` wins). So the Papercup persona is consistent across
voice / text / mobile.

## The read-context — it never waits on the Mug

The Papercup walks in already *knowing* the live system, so it can narrate (file +
nudge) instead of re-deriving from raw coord. It reads the **ready-made digests
directly** (D-009 — never a Mug-maintained status object, which would be stale
exactly when she is mid-turn, reintroducing the "wait on the Mug" problem the
Papercup exists to avoid). `papercup-context.ts` follows the `mug-brief.ts`
pattern exactly: a **pure deterministic renderer** (`renderSentinelContext`) over
already-shaped input + a **fail-soft deps adapter** (`gatherSentinelContext`, one
flaky leg degrades to an empty section, never throws). The four sources:

| Section | Source digest | Module |
|---|---|---|
| Live signals (escalations / blockers / decisions / completions, salience-ranked) | `curation:feed` | `gatherFleetSignals` + `rankFleetFeed` |
| Anomalies (detected drift + suggested action, severity-ordered) | Overwatch compute-brief | `computeOverwatchBrief` |
| Standing patterns + headline (recurring friction / sinks / deferrals / gaps) | `curation:state-of-pot` | `synthesizeStateOfHive` |
| Progress (live fleet load + liveness) | `fleet:assignments` | `listFleetAssignments` + `groupByAgent` |

It is a **Papercup slice** of the mug-brief — escalations/anomalies/progress +
"what's worth surfacing," **not** placement rank (the Mug owns placement; the
Papercup owns surfacing). Each section is capped (`DEFAULT_SENTINEL_CONTEXT_CAPS`) so
the block stays a digest; an all-quiet system renders the headings with an explicit
"nothing" so silence is a trustworthy signal, not an omission. It is injected into
the converse prompt's SYSTEM sections **only** when `role === 'papercup'` (the
operator path is byte-identical). mem0 is also injected into the Papercup converse
loop (`memory:search` at turn start, `memory:remember` for learnings, honoring the
EI-2032 auto-capture kill switch).

## Handoff to the Mug

When the user says "do it," the Papercup does **not** spawn a cup. It emits a
`<handoff_to_mug>` tag (parsed in `operator-converse-tags.ts`, dispatched by
`dispatchSentinelHandoff` in `operator-sentinel-handoff.ts` — the file/function
names kept their pre-rename `sentinel` spelling), which (D-003):

1. files a **high-priority `work_item`** tagged `user-requested`
   (`work_items:create { priority: high }`), and
2. **nudges the Mug** via `coord:send`/`escalate { to: mug, wake: true }`.

The Mug places it on her next wake — preserving the single-placer invariant while
giving the user-requested item visible priority. It is **tier-gated** (D-011): the
Papercup is the user-facing approval tier, reusing the existing standing-approval /
tier system (`operator-standing-candidates.ts`). **Low-tier** actions never reach
the user (the Mug auto-places); **medium/high-tier** un-approved actions surface
as a short voice/text approval prompt ("approve `<slug>`"). After handoff the
Papercup subscribes to the work_item thread and **reports the landing**; if the
session was away it surfaces the outcome via hindsight ("[While you were away]",
`notifyOperatorHindsight`). An invariant test asserts the Papercup **never** calls
`cup:spawn`.

## The settings tab — live overrides over workspace defaults

`PapercupTab.tsx` (renamed 2026-07-09 from `SentinelTab.tsx`) is the left-sidebar "quick live overrides" surface; the full
workspace settings hold the **defaults** (D-013). It is the **first consumer of the
shared `<OverridableSetting>` primitive** (D-016 / D-020 — not a 9th hand-rolled
badge/reset copy): each row shows an override-vs-workspace-default badge + a reset
(↺), precedence override > workspace default. Settings surfaced: audience mode
(engineer ↔ user-friendly, `audienceMode` `'engineer'`|`'novice'`, D-005),
voice on/off, proactive nudges (`proactiveTicksEnabled`), speak-status cadence
(`speakCadenceStatus`), and a do-not-disturb (`silenceVoice`). The override
read/write reuses the **voice-prefs workspace-default vs per-user-override seam**
(`mergeUserOverWorkspace` / `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`, the same `/settings/user`
pattern — no new store, D-014/A). The broader contract is documented in
[the unified override-settings backbone](/internal/docs/agent-insights/override-settings-backbone).

> Gotcha that bit during the build: `silenceVoice` / `audienceMode` /
> `proactiveTicksEnabled` were surfaced by the tab but were **absent from
> `VOICE_USER_OVERRIDE_KEYS`** (and `silenceVoice` was missing from
> `DEFAULT_VOICE_PREFS`), so the tab's overrides never reached the brain. If a new
> Papercup override doesn't take effect, check that its key is in the override-key
> set first.

## Proactive path — in progress (P-018-022)

The autonomous "decide to speak" loop is **not new** — it reuses the existing
active-mode proactive-tick engine + its full gate set (`proactiveTicksEnabled` /
`speakSuggestions` / `speakCadenceStatus`, pause / sleep / budget / DND /
single-speaker) and the `broadcastOpVoice → OPV_RESPONSE_AUDIO` injection seam
(D-007). The open work is **architectural** (D-008): the loop currently lives in
the **browser** React provider (`OperatorConversationProvider.tsx`), so it only runs
while the desktop UI is open. For a genuinely always-on Papercup that speaks with
**no UI open**, the proactive loop must move **server-side** (into the voice-node
host or a routine), with a single-owner guard so it does not double-fire when a
desktop provider is also running, re-aimed at Papercup fleet-status content and
routing voice-off alerts through `attention-notify` / `device-push-dispatcher`
(importance-gated), with hindsight on resume (D-010). This is P-018-022 and is still
in progress as of `papercup-herald-2026-06-21`.

## The old operator workspace-scan is retired (D-018)

The Papercup **replaces** the old scheduled operator workspace-scan (the "sweep +
surface ~5 next-action cards + auto-dispatch on a 4-hourly cron" surface). That
cadence is retired: the Mug scans/places continuously and the Papercup reads the
live blackboard directly. Concretely — the `scan` blueprint's `triggers.schedule`
was removed (so nothing materializes an active scan routine; the blueprint stays
launchable on-demand for a manual sweep, and its `improvements:capture` curation
path is unchanged), `seed-scan-routine.ts` is retired to a defensive deactivate-only
no-op, and the old operator-scan persona
(`blueprints/base/prompts/scanner.md`) is marked deprecated (its route was already
removed with the retired Next operator app; its tables dropped in migration 167).
Do not re-point the old scan at the Papercup — read the live digests instead.
